question: Evaluate $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)+\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5}{13}\right)+\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{56}{65}\right)$ exactly by establishing the required inverse-sine addition relation and verifying that the combined angle lies in the correct principal-value interval.
explanation:
Formation of Angles
Let
$$A=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right),\qquad B=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right)$$
Since both arguments are positive, $A$ and $B$ are positive acute principal angles. Therefore,
$$\sin A=\frac{3}{5},\qquad\cos A=\frac{4}{5}$$
and
$$\sin B=\frac{5}{13},\qquad\cos B=\frac{12}{13}$$

Applying the Addition Formula
Using the sine addition formula,
$$\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B$$
$$=\frac{3}{5}\cdot\frac{12}{13}+\frac{4}{5}\cdot\frac{5}{13}$$
$$=\frac{36}{65}+\frac{20}{65}=\frac{56}{65}$$
Also,
$$\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B$$
$$=\frac{4}{5}\cdot\frac{12}{13}-\frac{3}{5}\cdot\frac{5}{13}$$
$$=\frac{48}{65}-\frac{15}{65}=\frac{33}{65}>0$$
Since $A+B$ is positive and its cosine is positive, $A+B$ lies in $\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$. It therefore belongs to the principal-value range of $\sin^{-1}$. Hence,
$$A+B=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{56}{65}\right)$$

Evaluation
The required expression becomes
$$\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{56}{65}\right)+\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{56}{65}\right)$$
Using the property
$$\sin^{-1}t+\cos^{-1}t=\frac{\pi}{2},\qquad -1\leq t\leq1$$
we obtain
$$\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)+\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right)+\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{56}{65}\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}$$

Final Result
The exact value of the given expression is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
